name: Back Walk and Gowan Hill
text: Join the Back Walk opposite Stirling Central Library. This 3.3 km heritage walk follows the old town walls and climbs to views from Gowan Hill. Expect steps and some steep sections.

name: Airthrey Loch Circuit
text: Start at the university boatshed for a 2.3 km walk around Airthrey Loch. The circuit follows the waterfront past the golf pavilion to the quieter eastern end of the loch.

name: The Wallace Way
text: Start at the Wallace Monument visitor car park. This uphill woodland walk passes carved sculptures on Abbey Craig. Allow 15–20 minutes for the climb to the monument entrance, plus time to return.

name: Raploch River Walk
text: Join this four-mile riverside walk at Stirling Old Bridge, a landmark on the published route. The path follows the bends of the Forth around Raploch.

name: Solomon’s Temple from Buxton Station
text: Walk from Buxton railway station to the Victorian tower on Grin Low. The climb gives a view back across the town before the circular route returns to the station.

name: Corbar Cross from Buxton Station
text: Walk from Buxton railway station into Corbar Woods and climb to Corbar Cross. The route guide gives two approaches through the trees, including an alternative to the steep steps.

name: Georgian Buxton and Pavilion Gardens walk
text: Start at the west end of the Pavilion Gardens car park near Burlington Road. This town walk links the gardens, Georgian Buxton and the older streets of Higher Buxton.

name: Errwood Hall and the Shrine
text: Start at Errwood Hall car park for a three-mile walk in the Goyt Valley. The route links the ruins of the hall with the Grimshawe family burial ground and the little stone shrine.

name: Tideswell village history trail
text: Start and finish at Bank Square Garden. This self-guided heritage walk follows the village history trail through Tideswell, with a leaflet to help identify the stops.

name: Litton, Cressbrook Dale and the mills
text: Walk from Litton village green on a 7.9-mile circuit through Cressbrook Dale and Tideswell Dale. The route passes the former cotton mills and takes in part of the Monsal Trail.

name: Miller’s Dale Station to Tideswell and Wormhill
text: Start at Miller’s Dale Station for a 7.3-mile circular walk. Cross the Wye near Litton Mill, climb towards Tideswell, then return through Wormhill.

name: Cave Dale from Castleton Market Place
text: Walk from Castleton Market Place into the limestone gorge below Peveril Castle. The village guide describes an approximately one-hour circuit with steep, rough ground and exposed edges.

name: Mam Tor, Hollins Cross and Odin Mine
text: Start at Castleton visitor centre for a 5.4-mile heritage walk. It links the village with Hollins Cross, Mam Tor and the old road past Odin Mine.

name: Castleton village and surrounding fields
text: Start at Castleton visitor centre. This family walk follows village streets past Spital Bridge and returns through fields with views towards Mam Tor.

name: Great Ridge by train — Edale to Hope
text: Start at Edale Station for a one-way ridge walk over Mam Tor and Lose Hill, finishing in Hope. Plan the onward journey separately for this linear route.

name: Jubilee Walkway — Eastern Loop
text: Start outside Tate Modern for a 5.5 km circular walk along the Thames, taking in Tower Bridge and the Tower of London.

name: Jubilee Walkway — Westminster Loop
text: Start on the south side of Trafalgar Square. This 3 km circular walk links Westminster, St James’s Park and Buckingham Palace.

name: Little Venice to Camden
text: Walk from Little Venice towards Camden along the Regent’s Canal. The Canal & River Trust guide maps this linear route through London.

name: Diana Princess of Wales Memorial Walk
text: Begin at Kensington Palace for this seven-mile walk through four Royal Parks. Plaques set into the paths mark the circuit.

name: Montmartre village walk
text: Start outside Marché Saint-Pierre and walk up to Sacré-Cœur. The tourism office’s route returns through the streets of Montmartre to Place des Abbesses.

name: Île Saint-Louis and Île de la Cité
text: Start at Sully-Morland Métro. This city walk explores the quays and monuments of the two islands in the Seine.

name: Coulée verte René-Dumont
text: Join the walk on Avenue Daumesnil near Bastille. The landscaped former railway offers a green route through eastern Paris.

name: Lower Yosemite Fall loop
text: Start at the Lower Yosemite Fall trailhead. This one-mile loop leads to views of the waterfall.

name: Cook’s Meadow Loop
text: Join this one-mile meadow walk at the Lower Yosemite Fall shuttle stop. Open views take in Half Dome, Yosemite Falls and the valley walls.

name: Mirror Lake walk
text: Start at the Mirror Lake trailhead by shuttle stop 17. The lake-and-back walk is two miles, with a longer loop option in the park guide.

name: Yosemite Valley Loop Trail
text: Start at the Lower Yosemite Fall shuttle stop and walk west to join the Valley Loop Trail. This longer route traces historic paths and wagon roads on the valley floor.

name: Belfast Cave Hill Trail
text: Join the 7.2 km circular walk from the Belfast Castle estate to McArt’s Fort. The council lists 256 metres of ascent.

name: Belfast Castle Estate Trail
text: Walk the wooded lower slopes of Cave Hill from the Belfast Castle estate. This 3.9 km loop offers a shorter alternative to the summit trail.

name: Belfast Castle Garden Trail
text: This 1.3 km circular walk explores the gardens around Belfast Castle. The council guide distinguishes it from the longer woodland and hill routes.

name: Cardiff Bay Trail
text: Join the waterfront walking loop at Mermaid Quay. The 10 km circuit links Cardiff Bay and Penarth via the barrage and Pont y Werin.

name: Bute Park Champion Tree Trail
text: Enter Bute Park beside Cardiff Castle and use the park’s trail guide to locate its champion trees. This walk explores the park’s arboretum.

name: St Fagans Circular Walk
text: Use the council’s waymarked circular walk at St Fagans. The guide maps the route around this wooded area and flags a roadside verge on the northern section.

name: Rhymney Trail at Parc Tredelerch
text: Join the walking trail at Parc Tredelerch on Lamby Way. The council map shows the lake circuit and how the paths connect with the longer Rhymney Trail.
